On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines excluding emails already in booking.attendees) removes all previously-submitted guests and uniqueGuests.length === 0 triggers TRPCError BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', misleading the user while the calendar was never updated. Email sending is also swallowed by a bare console.log. All steps are verifiable

judged_text: addGuests performs three non-transactional side effects in sequence — attendee createMany (92-106), calendar update (165), emails (168) — with no compensation or rollback on failure. A failure in updateCalendarAttendees 500s the request after attendees are already persisted; the user's retry with the same valid emails then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' (lines 80-81), reporting their valid input as invalid, and nobody can tell the calendar was never updated.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] addGuests performs three non-transactional side effects in sequence — attendee createMany (92-106), calendar update (165), emails (168) — with no compensation or rollback on failure. A failure in updateCalendarAttendees 500s the request after attendees are already persisted; the user's retry with the same valid emails then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' (lines 80-81), reporting their valid input as invalid, and nobody can tell the calendar was never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` (lines ~92-106), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (line ~165) without a try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the request errors after DB state has been mutated. On retry with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out already-existing attendees (`!booking.attendees.some(...)`), so it becomes empty and triggers `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (lines ~80-81), even though the input emails are valid—exactly the inconsistent/irrecoverable state described. Emails are also sent after that (line ~168) with only email sending wrapped in try/catch, so no rollback occurs for earlier side effects.
